bars.name: Halo
bars.summary: Flat bar with a raised halo around the center item. Selection animates the icon and label.
bars.highlight: A flat bar with a raised, ringed center orb. Outlined/filled icon swap, spring bounce on selection, and a ring that ripples out of the orb when it is selected
intro: Each `HaloBarItem` takes a label, an icon, and an optional `selectedIcon` (usually the filled twin of the outlined icon). The **middle item becomes the halo**, so pass an odd number of items (3, 5, 7…).

notes.text: Any `ImageVector` works. The icons above come from `material-icons-extended`; the sample app draws its own.

The halo is a normal tab: selecting it swaps to its `selectedIcon`, and a ring ripples out of the orb. `onItemClick` also fires when the user taps the tab that is already selected, so you can scroll to the top or pop to the tab's root.

The bar is `BarHeight` (64dp) tall, and the halo rises `HaloOverhang` (22dp) above it, so leave that much room above the bar for the orb. `HaloBottomBarDefaults` also exposes `HaloSize`, `HaloRingWidth`, `IconSize` and `HaloIconSize`.

colors: Icon and label of the selected side tab
Icons of the other side tabs
Labels of the other side tabs

bars.name: Dome
bars.summary: Rounded bar whose top swells into a dome around a glowing orb. Labels slide in under the selected tab.
bars.highlight: A floating, rounded bar whose top edge swells into a dome around a glowing orb. Icon-only tabs; the selected one fills in and its label slides up underneath
intro: `DomeBarItem` works like `HaloBarItem`, and the **middle item becomes the orb** inside the dome, so pass an odd number of items. Side tabs show only their icon; the selected one switches to its `selectedIcon` and its label slides in underneath.
bars.usage:
val items = listOf(
    DomeBarItem("Home", Icons.Outlined.Home, Icons.Filled.Home),
    DomeBarItem("Search", Icons.Outlined.Search, Icons.Filled.Search),
    DomeBarItem("Store", Icons.Outlined.Storefront, Icons.Filled.Storefront), // the orb
    DomeBarItem("Cart", Icons.Outlined.ShoppingCart, Icons.Filled.ShoppingCart),
    DomeBarItem("Profile", Icons.Outlined.Person, Icons.Filled.Person),
)

DomeBottomBar(
    items = items,
    selectedIndex = selectedIndex,
    onItemClick = { selectedIndex = it },
    // All four corners are rounded, so it looks best floating a little above the screen edge.
    modifier = Modifier.padding(start = 12.dp, end = 12.dp, bottom = 12.dp),
    shadowElevation = 8.dp,
)

notes.text: The bar is `BarHeight` (66dp) tall plus `DomeRise` (28dp) for the dome, all inside its own bounds, so no extra room is needed above it. `shadowElevation` defaults to `0.dp`; the dome makes the outline concave, which Android can only cast a shadow for on API 30+.
Colors follow the same pattern, through `DomeBottomBarDefaults.colors(darkTheme)`, `lightColors(...)` and `darkColors(...)`:

bars.name: Socket
bars.summary: Floating pill whose selected icon lifts into a bubble, resting in a socket that glides from tab to tab.
bars.highlight: A floating pill where the selected icon lifts out of the bar into a bubble, resting in a socket cut into the top edge. Works with any number of tabs; the bubble and its socket glide from tab to tab
intro: `SocketBarItem` works like the others, but there is no center orb: **any tab can be selected into the bubble**, so pass any number of items (3 to 5 fit best). Every tab shows its label; the selected one's icon lifts into the bubble as its `selectedIcon`, and its label takes `selectedContentColor`.
bars.usage:
val items = listOf(
    SocketBarItem("Home", Icons.Outlined.Home, Icons.Filled.Home),
    SocketBarItem("Search", Icons.Outlined.Search, Icons.Filled.Search),
    SocketBarItem("Cart", Icons.Outlined.ShoppingCart, Icons.Filled.ShoppingCart),
    SocketBarItem("Profile", Icons.Outlined.Person, Icons.Filled.Person),
)

SocketBottomBar(
    items = items,
    selectedIndex = selectedIndex,
    onItemClick = { selectedIndex = it },
    // A floating pill, so keep it off the screen edges.
    modifier = Modifier.padding(horizontal = 16.dp, vertical = 12.dp),
)

notes.text: The pill is `BarHeight` (72dp) tall and the 52dp bubble (`BubbleSize`) rises `BubbleOverhang` (23dp) above it, all inside the bar's own bounds. The socket is shaped by `SocketGap` (the see-through ring around the bubble) and `SocketShoulderRadius`, and `ContentPadding` sets the space between the rounded ends and the outer tabs. The bar has no outer margin of its own, so pass one through `modifier`. As with the other cut-out bars, `shadowElevation` defaults to `0.dp` and needs API 30+ because of the concave outline.

installation.text: Compose Bottombar is published on [Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.nameisjayant/compose-bottombar). No extra repository is needed, just make sure `mavenCentral()` is listed (new Android projects include it by default):

lightDark.text: By default the bar follows `isSystemInDarkTheme()`. If your app has its own theme toggle, pass it in:

lightDark.code:
HaloBottomBar(
    items = items,
    selectedIndex = selectedIndex,
    onItemClick = { selectedIndex = it },
    colors = HaloBottomBarDefaults.colors(darkTheme = isDarkTheme),
)

customColors.text: Start from either palette and override only what you need:

customColors.code:
HaloBottomBar(
    items = items,
    selectedIndex = selectedIndex,
    onItemClick = { selectedIndex = it },
    colors = HaloBottomBarDefaults.lightColors(
        containerColor = Color(0xFFFFF8F0),
        selectedContentColor = Color(0xFFE85D3A),
        unselectedContentColor = Color(0xFFB8A99A),
        unselectedLabelColor = Color(0xFFB8A99A),
        haloColor = Color(0xFFE85D3A),
        haloRingColor = Color(0xFFFFC9B5),
        haloContentColor = Color.White,
    ),
)

labelStyle.code:
HaloBottomBar(
    items = items,
    selectedIndex = selectedIndex,
    onItemClick = { selectedIndex = it },
    labelStyle = HaloBottomBarDefaults.LabelStyle.copy(fontSize = 12.sp, fontFamily = MyFont),
    // The bar pads itself for the navigation bar by default. Pass zero insets when the parent already does.
    windowInsets = WindowInsets(0.dp),
)

navigation.text: The sample app gives each tab its own back stack with [Navigation 3](https://developer.android.com/guide/navigation/navigation-3), and switching tabs keeps every stack intact. Every bar is wired the same way:

navigation.code:
HaloBottomBar(
    items = tabs.map { it.item },
    selectedIndex = tabs.indexOfFirst { it.route == navigationState.topLevelRoute },
    onItemClick = { index -> navigator.navigate(tabs[index].route) },
)

navigation.text: See [`ShopTabsDemo.kt`](app/src/main/java/com/nameisjayant/composebottombar/demo/ShopTabsDemo.kt) for the full setup, shared by every bar's demo.

features: **Ready to use**: pass a list of items and the selected index, and you get a finished bar.
**Light and dark built in**: every bar ships both palettes and follows the system theme by default.

**Animated by default**: icon swaps, spring bounces, color fades and bar-specific touches like the Halo burst, the Dome's sliding labels, the Cradle's orb ripple, the Valley's orb press, the Socket's gliding bubble, the Gable's bubble sliding along its roof line, the Diamond's quarter-turn spin, the Wave's rings filling into solid orbs, the Rail's rails growing around the selected tab, the Crest's orb popping up as its wings dip, the Scribble's loop drawing itself around the selected icon, the Bead hopping from notch to notch, the Peak's strip stretching from tab to tab, the Teardrop popping out of its pointed tip, the ring rippling out of the Orbit's orb, the Tile stretching as it slides from tab to tab, the Arch sinking into the bar's edge and springing up under the next tab, the Satellite dot circling its orb as it glides to the next tab, the Spotlight panel stretching and resizing to fit the next label, the comet sweeping around the Collar's ring, the Buoy diving under the edge and resurfacing below the next tab or the Bloom orb blooming out of the icon as its label unrolls.
**Customizable**: change any color through `XxxBottomBarDefaults.lightColors(...)` / `darkColors(...)`, plus label style and window insets.
**Accessible**: items are exposed as selectable tabs in a selectable group, so TalkBack reads them correctly.
**Light dependencies**: only Compose UI, Foundation and Animation. No Material, icons or navigation library is forced on your app.
**Explicit API mode**, so the public API is exactly what is meant to be public.
